newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain union claims 43 bln pta in civil war seizure.
newsitem.headline: Spain union claims 43 bln pta in civil war seizure.

text.p: Spanish trade union UGT said it would present on Wednesday an official claim to the labour minister for payment of some 43 billion pesetas in compensation for properties and firms seized during the Spanish civil war.
"We will present around 3,000 records of cases...referring to land and properties, to cooperative firms and bank accounts," a spokesman for UGT told Reuters on Monday.
UGT's officials have worked for two years to prepare the documents supporting the union's view, and the amount requested includes interest re-payment and inflation.
Among others, the UGT claims repayment for properties of more than 22,000 square meters of Madrid land once on the outskirts and now home to some of Madrid's most expensive office buildings.
In addition, it is demanding repayment for drugstores in Madrid and Zaragoza, a cooperative for reduced-priced housing, other cooperative firms, and other assets UGT is claiming.
The Labour Ministry, which manages these assets, must then examine our documents, the source said.

"It is likely it will take a while for it to examine all documents. Afterwards, I imagine there will be talks to find an intermediate value. Then, it will be up to the cabinet minister to suggest the amount and the way they will pay back money to our organisation," the source at UGT said.
"Of course we do not expect the government will pay us this right away nor that they pay it in a lump sum," he said.
UGT has a 1997 budget forecasting 20.5 billion pesetas revenues and 19.2 billion pesetas in expenditures.
